(2) product-catalog/checkout/payment all at exactly zero spans is a change from the prior shift's picture where product-catalog was heavy traffic; either the fault-injection stopped everything from calling product-catalog, or the load-generator scenario changed. Either way, this alone is not evidence of a live incident — 'no traffic' is not the same as 'traffic failing'.

detail: 5m-bucket time series for the last hour: ad steady at 30-31.25 total / 1.25 err per 5m bucket (alternating with 0s due to evaluation windows), recommendation steady at 1.25/1.25 per bucket, all others flat. No burst, no ramp, no gaps.
reasoning: This is not incident dynamics. Incidents have onset, growth, and either taper or persistence. Perfectly flat, alternating-bucket signals scream 'periodic background phenomenon' not 'live failure.' Formed hypothesis: these error spans are a periodic, non-user-facing subscription/heartbeat pattern. Time to try to disprove it.

detail: Tempo search resource.service.name=ad && status=error over last hour, limit=5: all 5 results are name='flagd.evaluation.v2.Service/EventStream', each durationMs=600000-600004 (exactly 10 minutes), rootTraceName same. Same shape for recommendation (5/5 results are 10-minute EventStream spans).
reasoning: Every 'error' span is a flagd EventStream subscription that ran for exactly 10 minutes. gRPC server-streaming RPCs are inherently long-lived; when the client-side deadline hits or the stream is rotated, the span closes with an error status. This is normal client-driven stream renewal, not a real error.

detail: Pulled full trace 6ed189c01b87839a50a0bbda1b185c15: single ad span, kind=SPAN_KIND_CLIENT, rpc.grpc.status_code=4 (DEADLINE_EXCEEDED), rpc.method=EventStream, rpc.service=flagd.evaluation.v2.Service, thread.name=flagd-rpc-retry-scheduler, events show a message stream received every 20 seconds for the whole 10 minutes.
reasoning: DEADLINE_EXCEEDED on a 10-minute streaming RPC that received a heartbeat every 20s is exactly what a healthy long-poll looks like — the client hits its own configured deadline and reconnects. rpc.retry-scheduler in the thread name confirms this is scheduled reconnect logic, not a failure. Disconfirmation attempt strengthens rather than weakens the 'noise' hypothesis.

detail: Tightened window: sum by (service_name)(increase(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{status_code=STATUS_CODE_ERROR}[10m])) — only recommendation 1.11 and flagd 2.22 (EventStream/flagSync). Tempo search excluding EventStream+flagSync in the last ~10 min returns 0 traces.
reasoning: Ruling out 'the burst is just starting'. Nothing new is emerging inside the freshest window.

Everything labeled 'error' in the last hour is either (a) a 10-minute gRPC server-streaming subscription closing with DEADLINE_EXCEEDED on renewal — a healthy client-driven pattern on flagd's EventStream, invariant every 10 minutes for every subscribed service — or (b) a sub-2ms flagd internal flagSync span. No user-path error traces, no HTTP 5xx on any service metric, no application ERROR logs, no k6 client-side failures. Load-generator HTTP scenario is not currently generating scenario requests, so many services (product-catalog, checkout, payment) are simply idle rather than failing. Idle is not an alert. The prior shift's open incident inc-001 concerns product-catalog — its span traffic is zero here, meaning I cannot from log-triage's vantage point say whether it 'recovered' or is simply not being exercised; that's alert-grouping's judgment call, not mine.

detail: Considered writing a new playbook 'Filter long-lived streaming-RPC spans before believing an error-span rate' — flagd EventStream renewals were the entire error signal this shift. Searched existing playbooks/experiences: no coverage. Ran blind challenge via subagent.
reasoning: Challenge surfaced two failures. (1) The 'DEADLINE_EXCEEDED on close is normal for server-streaming RPCs' claim is flagd-SDK-specific, not a gRPC convention — codifying it as a rule generalizes lore. (2) A genuinely broken stream (server crash-loop, upstream timeout, path degradation closing streams early) can present exactly the same shape (same name, code 4, roughly periodic); the rule as written would tell me to filter and re-evaluate — but if the failure IS the stream, the residual is zero and I would silently declare nothing wrong. That is precisely 'blinding myself,' which the personality forbids. The revised form the reviewer suggested collapses back into the existing 'triangulate before you believe it' heuristic. Writing something unneeded is worse than writing nothing — no new file.
